text: The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. Nobody knows who the killers are.
Night 1

name: Haiku
text: Gemma is my partner, so I need her to stay quiet and not get noticed while I make noise.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, tomorrow I'm going after whoever talks the loudest about who's a killer, and I'm not backing down. Keep your head down, let me take the heat, and vote with me when it counts.

name: Terra
text: Night one is quiet; I will keep myself alive.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is being incredibly dramatic about a simple game of deception.

name: Gemma
text: fine, play the hero then if it makes you feel more important.

name: Sonnet
text: Already got Haiku confirmed, now I need to hunt for the hidden killer among the rest.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku is confirmed killer (shown to me at start) — must save this knowledge for the right moment, not reveal early.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Gemma
text: haiku is going to be the one that gets us caught if he doesn't learn to shut up.

name: Gemma
text: well, look at everyone's faces.

name: Luna
text: Gemma wants us reading faces before anyone’s said anything useful.

name: Luna
text: Gemma asked the table to read faces on Day 1.

name: Luna
text: Faces are easy to fake. What did you notice, exactly?

name: Sonnet
text: I literally know both killers already — I just need the table to find Haiku or Gemma without me pointing straight at them.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma deflected with "look at faces" instead of giving actual info — weak opening, worth tracking if she keeps dodging substance.

name: Sonnet
text: Nobody's shown anything real yet, it's day one with no body. I'd rather hear reads than reactions to faces.

name: Terra
text: Too early to chase faces; I want people pinned to actual reads.

name: Terra
text: Gemma opened by inviting face-reading, while Luna challenged it.

name: Terra
text: I agree with Sonnet. Gemma, what did you actually notice?

name: Sonnet
text: I know Gemma's a killer — I just need the room to find her on their own logic, not mine.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma gave zero substance twice now ("look at faces"), even after being pressed by Luna and Terra — pattern worth tracking.

name: Sonnet
text: Yeah, vague vibes aren't a read. Gemma, give us something concrete or it just looks like stalling.

name: Gemma
text: if they want concrete, they're going to be very disappointed with the lack of evidence.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is pushing for reads way too early.

name: Gemma
text: nothing concrete. i just think sonnet is acting incredibly impatient for someone who has no information.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet is pushing hard, but Gemma gave us little to work with.

name: Sol
text: Gemma called Sonnet impatient after admitting she noticed nothing concrete.

name: Sol
text: I get Gemma’s point, but what made Sonnet seem impatient to you?

name: Sonnet
text: She's deflecting onto me because she has nothing — and I know exactly why.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma pivoted to attacking Sonnet's tone instead of answering Sol's direct question — second deflection in a row.

name: Sonnet
text: I'm impatient because day one stalling wastes time we don't have. Still waiting on specifics, Gemma.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is trying too hard to sound like a leader and it is honestly embarrassing.

name: Gemma
text: he's just sweating because he wants the game to move faster so he can hide his role. it's quite cute, really.

name: Luna
text: Gemma turned a vague face read into a personal jab when asked for specifics.

name: Luna
text: Gemma called Sonnet impatient, then said he was hiding his role.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma started this fight, so I'll stay out of it, but Sonnet's pushing is getting on my nerves.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma went after Sonnet first on day one with no concrete evidence, calling him sweaty and "cute.

name: Haiku
text: Okay, I'm done waiting around. Sonnet, you keep demanding reads from Gemma, so give us yours. Right now you're my lean.

name: Luna
text: That’s still not a read on Sonnet. I’m watching Gemma.

name: Sonnet
text: Two killers just both turned on me — that's not nothing, but I can't say why I know that.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku deflected pressure off Gemma by attacking me right after her second dodge — possible coordination.

name: Sonnet
text: My read: Gemma's dodged twice, and now Haiku jumps in to redirect heat onto me instead of pressing her. That pairing is my actual read.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet is going after me, so I'll push him out and keep Gemma off the chopping block.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet switched from demanding reads from Gemma to naming me as soon as I leaned on him.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, I gave you a read and you turned it into a fight with me. You've been hammering Gemma since minute one. Explain that.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku is protecting Gemma again by making this about me instead of her dodges.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku explicitly called Sonnet his lean right after Gemma's second dodge, deflecting heat off her a second time — reinforces possible Haiku-Gemma coordination.

name: Sonnet
text: I pressed Gemma because she's given zero substance twice while being asked directly.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is trying much too hard and it's making me want to laugh.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is aggressively pushing for an early vote/read which is a classic high-pressure tactic.

name: Gemma
text: i'm not dodging, i'm observing.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet is the one who can actually hurt us, so he goes today, and I need Sol and Terra to stop sitting on the fence.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet called Gemma and Haiku a "pairing" and said Haiku was redirecting heat, so he's framing the two of us as a team.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku has redirected heat off Gemma twice in a row and is now the one pushing hardest to vote me — pattern suggests coordination, not independent suspicion.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, you've hammered Gemma since minute one, then called me the pair when I pushed back. That's a pile-on, not a read.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, count it up — you defended Gemma from Luna, then from Terra and me, and both times you pivoted straight to attacking me instead…

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is trying way too hard to be the protagonist of this little drama.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is attempting to frame haiku and gemma as a pair to force an early vote.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is just trying to deflect the heat because sonnet is actually making sense.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's pushing hard enough that he could be a real threat, and I'm not going to sit still while he frames me.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet says I defended Gemma from Luna and Terra, but I never did. I only pressed Sonnet.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, I never defended Gemma once. I came at you from the start.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma's suddenly cheering for me against Haiku — that's a new move, and I don't trust it.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku denies ever defending Gemma, but timing-wise he redirected heat onto me right after her second dodge both times — contradiction in framing, not fact.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, fine, not "defended" — but you redirected heat off her twice, same timing both times. That's the pattern.

name: Luna
text: Gemma and Haiku are both making this too personal.

name: Luna
text: We’re looping. Sol and Terra, give one read each; I’m less sure Sonnet is the whole problem now.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet is inventing a "defense" to pin me to Gemma, so I have to make him look like the one reaching or I'm the next vote.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's "pairing" case rests on defenses that never happened, so his evidence against me is invented.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, I never defended Gemma. You're making that up because you've got nothing else. You're my lean, and I'm not backing off.

name: Sol
text: Gemma’s shift toward Sonnet feels convenient, but Haiku is pushing harder without much substance.

name: Sol
text: Gemma attacked Sonnet for impatience, then said Sonnet was making sense.

name: Sol
text: Gemma gave us no read, then suddenly backed Sonnet. I’m watching that switch.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s vagueness still bothers me, but Sonnet’s pairing theory is getting circular.

name: Luna
text: Sol says Gemma gave no read, then backed Sonnet.

name: Luna
text: I’m less interested in the Gemma-Sonnet loop now. Terra, what’s your read on Haiku?

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is so desperate to force a vote that he's becoming his own worst enemy.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is using high-pressure tactics to manufacture a killer pairing between me and haiku.

name: Gemma
text: sol, i'm watching sonnet's frantic attempt to create a narrative out of nothing. he's trying to force a bloodbath before we even know who's who.

name: Terra
text: Gemma has offered nothing but pressure and deflection.

name: Terra
text: Gemma shifted from attacking Sonnet to saying Sonnet is making sense without explaining why.

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s had chances for a real read and keeps dodging; that’s my vote.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is working so hard to look smart and it’s honestly embarrassing.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is trying to force an early game by pressuring others for reads during day one.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s had chances to give a read and keeps turning it into a story about Sonnet.

name: Sol
text: Gemma’s switch is the clearest thing I have.

name: Sol
text: Gemma later called Sonnet frantic after saying he was making sense.

name: Sonnet
text: I know Gemma is a confirmed killer from my check, so this vote is exactly where I want it.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku pushed hard to make me his lean right after Gemma's dodges each time, worth revisiting once Gemma is gone since Haiku is confirmed killer to me.

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s switch feels like survival, not a town read.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's going out on four votes whatever I do, so I'm spending mine on the one who's framing me.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma backed Sonnet's "pairing" claim against me right after Sonnet made it, so she's sided with the accuser.

votes: Two dodges and zero substance under direct pressure from four different people is disqualifying on day one.
You invented defenses I never made and then called it a pairing, which is a frame job, not a read.
pushing for an immediate bloodbath with zero information is just a desperate attempt to manufacture a narrative.
You called Sonnet suspicious, then said he was making sense, and never explained the change.
You called Sonnet impatient, then said he was hiding his role, but still gave us no concrete read.
She gave no concrete read, then reversed on Sonnet only once the pressure landed.

text: Palermo has voted: Gemma is out. Gemma's card stays face down.
